items.title: Energy Secretary Wright says Hormuz tanker traffic could resume within weeks

featured_image.name: Energy Secretary Says Tankers Could Start Moving Soon - The New York Times

items.description:
U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Sunday that an oil tanker had successfully passed through the Strait of Hormuz, offering the first glimmer of hope that the critical waterway could resume regular shipping after being effectively shut down for nearly a week following U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran.

"We're not too long away, I think, before you'll see more regular resumption of ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz," Wright said on CNN's "State of the Union," adding that in a "worst case" scenario, full resumption could take "a few weeks, that's not months."[1][2]

items.title: Iran war hits civilian infrastructure as Mojtaba Khamenei named supreme leader

featured_image.name: Iran clerics name Khamenei's son as next supreme leader

items.description: The nine-day-old war between the U.S.-Israeli coalition and Iran widened into civilian infrastructure on Sunday as both sides struck energy and water facilities, while Iranian state television announced that Mojtaba Khamenei has been named the country's new supreme leader, succeeding his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in the opening strikes of the conflict on February 28.[1][2]

items.title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine recaptured up to 435 sq km in south

featured_image.name: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy says forces advancing ‘in all directions’

items.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced on March 8 that Ukrainian defense forces have recaptured between 400 and 435 square kilometers of territory in southern Ukraine over the past six weeks, calling the campaign a success in disrupting Russian military plans in the region.

items.title: Iran war widens as Bahrain reports desalination plant struck, Saudi Arabia sees first deaths

featured_image.name: Is Iran expanding attacks to target energy and civilian sites in the Gulf?

items.description: The war between Iran and a U.S.-Israeli coalition widened into attacks on civilian infrastructure on Sunday as Bahrain accused Iran of striking a desalination plant and Saudi Arabia reported its first fatalities in the nine-day-old conflict.

items.title: Iran names Mojtaba Khamenei as new supreme leader

featured_image.name: Iran War: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei's Son, Mojtaba, Chosen as Next Supreme  Leader - Bloomberg

items.description: Iran's Assembly of Experts has selected Mojtaba Khamenei, the 56-year-old son of the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, as the country's new Supreme Leader, according to Reuters and Iranian state media reports on Sunday. The appointment marks the first hereditary transfer of power in the Islamic Republic's history — a system founded in 1979 on the explicit rejection of monarchy.[1][2]

items.title: Iran reaffirms military alliance with Russia as war intensifies

featured_image.name: Minister: Iran to respond forcefully to any 'transgression'

items.description:
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Sunday dismissed growing international calls for a ceasefire in the country's widening war with the United States and Israel, declaring Tehran will keep fighting until it secures a lasting end to hostilities. The remarks, made during an appearance on NBC's "Meet the Press," came as the conflict entered its second week with no signs of abating and Iran moved closer to naming a successor to the slain Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.[1][2]

"There should be a permanent end of the war. And unless we get to that, I think we need to continue fighting for the sake of our people and our security," Araghchi said. He directly rejected President Trump's demand for Iran's unconditional surrender, drawing a comparison to last year's 12-day conflict with Israel. "We resisted, and after 12 days the Israelis asked for an unconditional ceasefire. So we never give up. We never surrender".[3]

items.title: Apple's 50th anniversary kicks off with museum exhibit, new book

featured_image.name: Tim Cook reflects on Apple's 50-year history

items.description: As April 1 draws near, Apple is preparing to mark a half-century since Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne founded Apple Computer Company in a Los Altos, California, garage in 1976. The milestone has prompted an unusual wave of reflection from a company long known for looking forward rather than back.

items.title: Trump rebuffs UK carrier readiness, says US 'already won' Iran war

featured_image.name: Keir Starmer channels Top Gun on visit to Britain's flagship aircraft  carrier as PM issues 'new era' warning | The Standard

items.description:
President Donald Trump publicly dismissed Britain's move to ready its aircraft carrier for possible deployment to the Middle East on Saturday, declaring the United States has "already won" its war with Iran and does not need belated help from its closest ally.

"The United Kingdom, our once Great Ally, maybe the Greatest of them all, is finally giving serious thought to sending two aircraft carriers to the Middle East," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "That's OK, Prime Minister Starmer, we don't need them any longer — But we will remember. We don't need people that join Wars after we've already won!"[1][2]

The broadside came shortly after the UK Ministry of Defence announced it had halved the deployment readiness window for HMS Prince of Wales, the Royal Navy's flagship carrier, from 10 days to five, according to Sky News. A British official said no final decision had been made on sending the carrier to the region.[2][3]

items.title: Toxic black rain blankets Tehran after Israeli strikes on oil depots

featured_image.name: Iran war live: Israel hits Tehran oil depots; 2 killed in Saudi Arabia

items.description:
Tehran awoke Sunday morning to an apocalyptic scene: thick black clouds blocking out the sun and oil-saturated rain falling across Iran's capital after Israeli airstrikes destroyed multiple fuel storage facilities overnight. The Iranian Red Crescent issued urgent warnings to the city's residents, saying the fires had released "significant quantities of toxic hydrocarbon compounds, sulfur, and nitrogen oxides" into the atmosphere.[1][2]

"In the event of precipitation, the resulting rain is extremely dangerous and highly acidic," the Red Crescent said in a statement, warning that exposure could cause skin burns and severe lung damage.[3][2]

items.title: Israel strikes Tehran oil sites as Trump demands Iran's surrender

featured_image.name: Iran oil facilities hit for first time as war with US-Israel enters day 9

items.description: On February 28, 2026, the United States and Israel launched a coordinated military assault on Iran that killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and dozens of senior military and political officials, plunging the Middle East into its most volatile conflict in decades. Now entering its ninth day, the campaign — dubbed Operation Epic Fury by the U.S. and Operation Roaring Lion by Israel — has reshaped the region's security landscape with no end in sight.

items.title: Iran threatens to strike regional oil sites after Israel hits Tehran fuel depots

featured_image.name: Tehran plunged into midday blackout from Israeli strikes on oil depots

items.description: Iran's military command threatened on Sunday to strike oil facilities across the Middle East if Israel continues its attacks on the Islamic Republic's energy infrastructure, warning that oil prices could surge above $200 per barrel. The threat came as Tehran residents woke to skies choked with toxic black smoke and acidic rainfall after Israeli warplanes hit multiple fuel depots in and around the Iranian capital overnight.

items.title: Israel says it killed Iran's new military bureau chief in Tehran strike

featured_image.name: Israeli military says it has begun a new wave of strikes on Tehran | Reuters

items.description: The Israeli military announced Sunday that it killed Abu al-Qassem Baba'iyan, the newly appointed head of the military bureau of Iran's supreme leader, in a precision airstrike in Tehran on Saturday. The strike represents the latest in a systematic Israeli campaign to dismantle Iran's senior military command structure since the start of hostilities on February 28.

items.title: Russia says it intercepted 170 Ukrainian drones in four hours

featured_image.name: Russia's drone revolution heaps pressure on Ukrainian ...

items.description:
Russia's Defense Ministry said on Sunday that its air defense units intercepted 170 Ukrainian drones over central and southern Russia within a four-hour window, in what officials described as a higher-than-average wave of aerial attacks that included two drones headed for Moscow.[1][2]

The interceptions took place between 2 p.m. and 6 p.m. Moscow time (1100-1500 GMT), according to the ministry. The Bryansk region, which borders Ukraine, recorded the highest concentration with 73 drones intercepted. No damage or casualties were reported.[3][4]

items.title: US, Israel weigh special forces raid to seize Iran's enriched uranium

featured_image.name: U.S. weighs sending special forces to seize Iran's nuclear ...

items.description: The United States and Israel have discussed sending special forces into Iran to secure its stockpile of highly enriched uranium at a later stage of the ongoing war, Axios reported Saturday, citing four sources with knowledge of the discussions. The operation, one of the most sensitive options under consideration, would require American or Israeli troops to enter heavily fortified underground nuclear facilities on Iranian soil.[1][2]

items.title: UAE denies Israeli reports it struck Iranian desalination plant

featured_image.name: UAE denies striking Iran water facility after Gulf attacks ...

items.description: Multiple Israeli media outlets reported Sunday that the United Arab Emirates carried out its first offensive strike against Iran, targeting a desalination facility — a claim the UAE swiftly and categorically denied, calling the reports "fake news" and "inappropriate."

items.title: Israel says it dropped 7,500 bombs on Iran in first week of war

featured_image.name: Netanyahu tells Iranians freedom is near as Israel hits ...

items.description:
The Israeli military announced that it has conducted approximately 3,400 strikes across Iran and dropped roughly 7,500 munitions since the war began on February 28, marking a dramatic escalation in the joint U.S.-Israeli campaign dubbed Operation Roaring Lion.[1][2]

IDF Spokesman Brig. Gen. Effie Defrin detailed the scope of the campaign in a press conference on Friday, noting that the munitions total is "twice the number dropped during Operation Rising Lion," referring to Israel's 12-day war with Iran in June 2025. The IDF also said more than 150 Iranian air defense systems have been disabled since the operation's launch.[2][1]

items.title: Saudi Arabia reports first deaths as projectile hits Al-Kharj

featured_image.name: Military projectile hits residential site in Al-Kharj, two ...

items.description:
A military projectile struck a residential compound in Al-Kharj, Saudi Arabia, on Sunday, killing two foreign nationals and injuring 12 others in what officials confirmed were the kingdom's first civilian deaths since the US-Israel-Iran war began on February 28.

The Saudi Civil Defense said the projectile hit a residential site belonging to a maintenance and cleaning company, killing one Indian national and one Bangladeshi national. The 12 injured were all Bangladeshi residents. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said earlier on Sunday that they had targeted radar systems at locations including Al-Kharj, which is home to Prince Sultan Air Base, a key US military facility that has been repeatedly targeted since the war began.[1][2][3][4][5][6][7]

items.title: Israeli airstrike kills 2 in Gaza amid ongoing ceasefire breaches

featured_image.name: Israeli attack across Gaza kill 14 Palestinians despite 'ceasefire'

items.description:
An Israeli airstrike killed at least two Palestinians traveling in a vehicle near Al-Azhar University in western Gaza City on Sunday, according to Reuters and local health authorities, marking the deadliest single incident in the territory since the U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran began a week earlier.[1][2]

Medical officials said several other people in the area were also wounded in the strike. The identities of the two victims have not been confirmed. The Israeli military did not comment on the attack.[1]

items.title: Iran missile with suspected cluster warhead wounds six in central Israel

featured_image.name: 6 wounded by shrapnel, 1 seriously, as Iran fires suspected cluster warhead  missile at Israel | The Times of Israel

items.description: An Iranian ballistic missile carrying a suspected cluster warhead struck central Israel on Sunday afternoon, wounding six people at multiple impact sites across the Tel Aviv metropolitan area, as the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its ninth day.

items.title: Israeli settlers murder three Palestinians in West Bank village raid

featured_image.name: Israeli Settler Attack in West Bank Kills Three Palestinians

items.description: Three Palestinians were killed and several others wounded when Israeli settlers stormed the village of Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, in an overnight attack early Sunday, marking the second deadly settler shooting in the occupied West Bank in as many days.
